invariants.rationale: The method operates on 'tooltip' directly; it is likely non-null when the method exits.
showTask.cancel() is called unconditionally, so at method exit, showTask should no longer be scheduled.
If the tooltip's container had a parent (and thus we entered the if), shown.removeValue(tooltip, true) was called, implying it is no longer in 'shown'.
If tooltip.container has a parent, resetTask is scheduled before method exit.
